en.headline: Hong Kong Arts Festival website reports unauthorised access to ticket buyer data
en.dek: The organisers said personal data of several thousand advance ticket buyers for the 55th festival may have been accessed after detecting a breach on 23 November.
body: The Hong Kong Arts Festival Society said it detected unauthorised access to its main website on 23 November and has reported the incident to the police and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data.

According to the organisers, initial investigations suggest that personal data of several thousand people who made advance bookings for the 55th Hong Kong Arts Festival may have been unlawfully accessed. The data potentially includes names, telephone numbers, email addresses, mailing addresses and credit card numbers, though not the card security codes.

The society said it had worked with its outsourced website and cloud hosting contractor to investigate and had taken immediate steps to prevent further unauthorised access. It has emailed potentially affected ticket buyers to inform them of the incident and expressed apologies for any inconvenience or concern caused.

As of early Thursday, the Hong Kong Arts Festival website displayed a notice that it was undergoing system maintenance and was temporarily unavailable. The organisers said they would fully cooperate with investigations and take appropriate measures to prevent similar incidents.

zh.headline: 香港藝術節網站遭入侵 數千名購票者資料或被非法閱覽
zh.dek: 主辦方表示11月23日發現主網站被未經授權進入，初步懷疑數千名第55屆藝術節門票預訂觀眾的個人資料可能外洩。
body: 香港藝術節協會表示，於11月23日發現主網站遭未經授權的第三方入侵，已向警方報案及通報個人資料私隱專員公署，並對事件深表歉意。
根據初步調查，懷疑數千名第55屆藝術節門票預訂觀眾的個人資料可能曾被未經授權人士非法閱覽，資料可能包括姓名、電話、電郵地址、郵寄地址及信用卡號碼，但不包括信用卡安全碼。
協會已與外判網站服務及雲端託管承辦商深入調查，並即時採取措施防止再次非法入侵。協會已透過電郵通知可能受影響的觀眾，並呼籲他們對來歷不明的聯絡提高警覺。
截至星期四凌晨，香港藝術節網站顯示正進行系統維護，暫停服務。主辦方表示會全力配合調查，並採取適當措施防止同類事件再次發生。
